summary: After the broker drops the socket, nothing of the last connection carries over: the first tk after the reconnect has no feed time, and the frame leaves ltt out rather than pass a receipt time off as one. The next tf with a time brings ltt back, and a partial tf after it keeps that time.

notes: Partial updates overlay within a connection only: docs/port/market-data-frames.md, Partial-update feeds; lead correction 2026-11-09, .lane/107/decisions.md: a field a partial packet omits is unchanged, not unknown. Both sides drop their snapshots on a new connection.
Lead ruling (round 3 review): on a partial-update feed, no trade time yet in this connection means ltt is left out; a receipt time is never passed off as a trade time.

deviations.reason: The first tk of the new connection has no feed time; the web's snapshot was cleared and it sends ltt as an empty string. With no trade time yet on this connection the desktop leaves ltt out rather than pass a receipt time off as one.

The web sends AliceBlue's feed time ft unchanged as ltt: epoch seconds, as a string; feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends the time in ms, as a number.

AliceBlue's tick carries last_quantity (ltq); the web's mapper never reads it (aliceblue_mapping.py:111-217), so its Quote leaves out a value the broker sent (lost data, lead ruling 2026-11-09). The desktop sends it.
